description.short_caption: Peripheral blood smear showing red blood cells with central pallor.
description.detailed_description: This is a peripheral blood smear under light microscopy. The image shows numerous red blood cells, many of which exhibit central pallor, consistent with their biconcave shape. There are no visible white blood cells or platelets in this field. The smear appears to be stained with a standard hematologic stain, such as Wright-Giemsa.
visible_findings: central pallor in red blood cells
absence of visible white blood cells or platelets in this field

description.short_caption: Blood smear showing intraerythrocytic parasite consistent with Plasmodium species.
description.detailed_description: This image is a stained blood smear under light microscopy, showing numerous red blood cells. One cell contains a visible intraerythrocytic parasite, likely a Plasmodium species, characterized by a purple-stained structure within the cell. The smear provides evidence of parasitic infection, such as malaria. The background is clear, with no significant debris or artifacts.
visible_findings: purple-stained structure within a red blood cell
